items.stem:
Read the following extract on theories of intelligence and answer the questions that follow.
"Gardner proposed eight types of intelligence that are independent of each other but interact. Thurstone proposed seven primary mental abilities, including verbal comprehension, numerical ability, spatial relations and memory. Sternberg's experiential intelligence involves the use of past experiences creatively to solve novel problems."
(i) Guilford's structure-of-intellect model has a total of: (1)
(ii) Explain the term 'triarchic theory' as it relates to this theme. (1)
(iii) Explain the reason behind the following: Gardner's theory has been influential in education. (2)
items.answer: (i) 180 cells (ii) Robert Sternberg's theory that intelligence has three components: componential, experiential and contextual. (iii) It shows that students may be strong in different kinds of intelligence, such as music or interpersonal skills, not only in language and logic.
items.markingKey: 1+1+2 marks: (i) 180 cells (ii) Robert Sternberg's theory that intelligence has three components: componential, experiential and contextual. (iii) It shows that students may be strong in different kinds of intelligence, such as music or interpersonal skills, not only in language and logic.

items.stem: Distinguish between 'two-factor theory' and 'primary mental abilities'.
items.answer: Two-factor theory: Charles Spearman's theory that intelligence consists of a general factor (g) and specific factors (s). Primary mental abilities: Louis Thurstone's theory that intelligence consists of seven primary abilities, such as verbal comprehension and numerical ability.
